topics: Equation 1.27 versus printed 1.32 sign audit and Fourier symbols

records.summary: The chat developed a historical numerical programme from exact linear propagation and weighted-decay studies into nonlinear profile experiments and one-input optical PINN validation. It produced multiple reports and visualizations, then reviewed long periodic reference trajectories. The final discussion emphasizes formulation fidelity, finite-time evidence, per-input retraining and the limits of peak/loss-only claims.
results: Canonical Gaussian weighted peak searches reached t = 1024; restricted-input studies completed 40 screened records after retained follow-ups. (Recorded historical CPU numerical evidence; no theorem or counterexample.)

28 discrete spatial Dysthe traveling profiles and refined collision/perturbation tests were reported; optical stripe perturbations were resolved through t = 4 but later t = 8 remained unresolved. (Different nonlinear formulations explicitly separated.)

The original 90-degree two-packet pair has zero intensity cross-term under the real-coefficient canonical propagator; an in-phase control demonstrates interference. (Interpretation correction preserved alongside earlier figures.)

One optical PINN completed 20,000 A100 steps; independent short-time evaluation reports 0.665 percent maximum relative complex-field error over 0 <= t <= 0.5. (One input/seed benchmark; not generalization or a long-time result.)

An optical reference run reached t = 8 but its sampled peak-grid discrepancy 0.795 percent exceeded the 0.5 percent gate although field/time checks passed. (Reference peak-resolution failure; not PINN-training failure.)

A periodic optical fine-step run reached t = 2048 in about 5.12 h with maximum relative mass drift 7.39e-12; long-time grid/time accuracy was not validated. (Completed reference trajectory, accuracy unresolved.)
A separate coarse optical preview targeting t = 12288 stopped at t = 10321 after relative mass drift exceeded 0.1 percent. (Stopped diagnostic-limited preview; not blow-up or completed target.)
Local four-harmonic fit on 1536 <= t <= 1664 has recorded R2 about 0.985 and base period 11.48. (Descriptive local fit; no future prediction, decay law or proof of breather.)
unresolved: No new uniform decay theorem or certified counterexample.
Long optical trajectories lack independent late-time grid/time refinement; mass conservation alone does not validate them.
Breathing-like peak modulation does not establish a localized breather without spatial/phase evidence.
The trained historical PINN fits one prescribed input and requires retraining for changed initial data.
No calibrated measured-data propagation benchmark was completed.
Optical and canonical branches are historical under current water-wave scope.

topics: Continued smoothness and finite-time numerical evidence for water-wave Dysthe
Original 1979 and 2026 preprint equation audits
Spatial free-surface Fourier reference, differentiable operators, FNO/PINO and per-inlet slab PINNs
CPU-to-cluster tests, longer propagation, derivative-sensitive errors and random-input failures
Soliton/coherent-wave literature and resolution limits
Separately versioned original-paper temporal potential-envelope study

results: October 23: 12-page existence review recommends a numerical reference plus spectral PINN, with analytical validation required for any existence certificate; audits 1979 and 2026 equations.
October 25: 18-page operator-learning review with 22 references and ten test protocols; methods from the separate NLS literature review are adapted to Dysthe's derivative and nonlocal terms.

October 26: CPU pilot found four-slab per-inlet PINNs strongest among tested neural methods through xi = 2 (0.963% worst complex-field, 1.881% H1); FNO/PINO failed declared gates and the numerical solver remained faster and more accurate. Code and A100 workflow were published.
October 26: staged spatial numerical xi = 4,8,16,32,64 and PINN xi = 4,8,16 tests, twelve inlets/three seeds, H2/refinement/domain checks and Slurm arrays published at c04b44b.

October 27: soliton/test report expanded after cluster results arrived: twelve numerical cases reported qualified through xi = 64; none of 24 evaluated PINN fits passed combined xi = 4 criteria; twelve random fits had execution errors; packet domain checks passed xi = 4 and failed xi = 8.

October 27: checksummed inlet reuse repaired cross-node random-data failures; Fourier coefficient conditioning retained 48 modes/full physics and reduced one-seed CPU H2 errors through xi = 4 from 26.11/12.11/15.85% to 1.47/0.65/0.22% for packet/sideband/random. Seventy-two local tests were reported; learning and experiment repair branches pushed.

October 29-30: returned to original 1979 temporal velocity-potential equation; preserved c = 1 literal-print versus c = 3/2 stability-consistent discrepancy as explicit versions. Six primary temporal cases passed refinement through T = 16; a 20-page report and forwardable proof of concept were delivered.

October 30: recreated historical visual style for new one-coordinate temporal trajectories; seven-page report/nine figures and animation. CPU nonlinear comparisons through T = 4, near-zero snapshots 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2, and direct periodic linear snapshots through T = 1024 completed.
October 30: separate periodic and isolated-domain nonlinear ladders 16..1024 prepared and small execution tests passed. The distant nonlinear targets were explicitly unrun.

November 5: current user request asks to compile all work with dates/experiment names to GitHub and to include every project chat, including unrelated conversations; this publication turn is still in progress.
unresolved: Global smooth existence remains an analytical question; finite-grid smooth trajectories and small PINN residuals do not prove it.
Improved spatial PINN reruns need cluster verification across seeds/horizons; the completed repair evidence is CPU and one-seed.
Nonlinear temporal T = 1024 remains a prepared target, subject to convergence/domain/physical-validity checks.
NOAA was only a vague future direction; no buoy, depth or phase-complete data comparison has been selected.
Temporal and spatial formulations, ordinary versus historical weighted norms, and isolated versus periodic conclusions must remain separate.
